newsitem.title: MEXICO: Banamex sees 16 pct end-1996 capital ratio.
newsitem.headline: Banamex sees 16 pct end-1996 capital ratio.

text.p: Grupo Financiero Banamex-Accival Grupo Financiero Banamex Accival SA de CV Director General Manuel Medina Mora said the bank is expected to end 1996 with a capitalization ratio of 16 percent.

"In these last 12 months, our group (increased) its capital base by $1.1 billion so that we can end the year with one of the highest capitalizations in the Mexican system, 16 percent," he told reporters.
At the end of 1995, Banamex's capitalization ratio was 11.7 percent.
In a year-end speech to reporters, Medina Mora said the process of recapitalizing the bank was "practically finished", and had not involved dilution for the bank's shareholders.
He also said the problem of past-due loans was stabilizing, even though he acknowledged it was "still far from being fully resolved."

Mexican banks were plunged into crisis when interest rates soared last year in the wake of the December 1994 peso devaluation. The government has pumped in resources to bail them out and the banks have also made their own efforts to booost capital levels and reserves.
